tests.name: MRSA
tests.description: Most MRSA infections are healthcare-associated, but an increasing number of infections are community- acquired, with patients having no established risk factors for acquisition of MRSA. While infections with community-acquired MRSA (CA-MRSA) are usually mild they can be severe.

specimen.specimen_type_raw:
Swab from Nose, Groin and manipulated wound sites. Perineal swabs will be accepted if agreed with your local IPC Team. Urine, Sputum and manipulated sites will be accepted if they are within local guidance and agreed with the IPC Team. Double MRSA eSwab (nose & groin/perineum only)

Single eSwab (wound sites)

NOTE: Urine sample requested for MRSA screen must be sent in urine boric acid container (below)
specimen.container: Collection using Liquid eSwabs under the direction of your local IPC Team.
specimen.minimum_volume_raw:
1ml. Liquid eSwabs contain 1ml of liquid. No liquid should be discarded when collecting sample. Samples with insufficient liquid will be discarded

Bacteriology
specimen.collection:
Use aseptic technique Double MRSA eSwab (N+G, or Peri): Dampen swab with one drop of sterile saline. Do not use the liquid from the eSwab as the whole amount is needed for the test. Do not use excessive force, pressure or bending when collecting the swab or it could break. Apply label vertically.

Bacteriology

Single MRSA eSWAB (all other sites): Dampen swab with one drop of sterile saline. Do not use the liquid from the eSwab as the whole amount is needed for the test. Do not use excessive force, pressure or bending when collecting the swab or it could break

Liquid eSwabs contain 1ml of liquid. No liquid should be discarded when collecting sample. Samples with insufficient liquid will be discarded.
specimen.transport: Specimens should be transported and processed as soon as possible.
specimen.special_precautions:
If processing is delayed, refrigeration is preferable to storage at ambient temperature. Delays of over 48hr are undesirable. The white swabs should be used for nose swab as nose is the highest area of MRSA colonisation. The white swab swab should remain in the sample tube and is transferred to the laboratory.

Pink swab should NEVER transferred to the lab.

analysis.interferences: Collect specimens before antimicrobial therapy where possible.

turnaround.raw: Negative screen at 1 working day Positive MRSA result with sensitivities at 2 working days
